subject: storytime
title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
about: Beatrix Potter's 1902 classic about the naughty bunny who sneaks into Mr. McGregor's garden, loses his shoes and his jacket, and gets home to bed with a cup of tea. This is a short retelling in first-grade words that keeps a few of Potter's own famous lines; the book itself is in the public domain, so he can meet the real one at the library afterwards. Five pages long.
tip: Ask: what did Peter's mother tell him, and what did he do instead?

book.author: Beatrix Potter (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A naughty bunny in Mr. McGregor's garden.

passage.text:
Once upon a time there were four little rabbits.
Their names were Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter.
They lived under a big fir tree.
"Now run along," said Mrs. Rabbit.
"But do not go into Mr. McGregor's garden."
"And don't get into mischief."
Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail were good little bunnies.
They went to pick blackberries.
But Peter was very naughty.
He ran straight to Mr. McGregor's garden!
***
First he ate some lettuces.
Then he ate some beans.
Then he ate some radishes.
He felt rather sick.
So he went to look for some parsley.
At the end of the row was Mr. McGregor!
Mr. McGregor jumped up.
He ran after Peter, waving a rake.
"Stop, thief!" he called.
***
Peter was very scared.
He ran all over the garden.
He lost one shoe in the cabbages.
He lost the other in the potatoes.
Then he ran into a net!
The big buttons on his jacket got stuck.
He shed big tears.
Some sparrows flew to him.
"Try, try again!" they said.
***
Mr. McGregor came with a sieve.
He tried to pop it on Peter.
But Peter wriggled out just in time.
He left his jacket behind.
He ran into the tool shed.
He hid in a can of water!
Then Peter sneezed.
Mr. McGregor heard him.
He ran after Peter again.
Peter jumped out of a window.
Mr. McGregor got tired of running.
He went back to his work.
***
Peter ran and ran.
He did not stop till he got home.
He flopped down on the soft sand.
He was not very well that evening.
His mother put him to bed.
She made him a cup of tea.
But Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread and milk.
And blackberries for supper.

cards.q: Who was the naughty little rabbit?
cards.note: Four bunnies: Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail and Peter, and only one of them is naughty.

cards.q: Which place did Mrs. Rabbit say to stay out of?
cards.note: His mother said it plainly, and he went straight there anyway.

cards.q: What did Mr. McGregor do when he saw Peter?
cards.note: Stop, thief! A thief is someone who takes what is not theirs, like Peter and the lettuces.

cards.q: What did Peter lose in the garden?
cards.note: One shoe in the cabbages, one in the potatoes, and the jacket caught on the net.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Mrs. Rabbit's warning comes first, which is what makes Peter naughty.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Peter got tea in bed; the good bunnies got bread, milk and blackberries.

cards.q: How did Peter feel when he saw Mr. McGregor?
cards.note: So scared he ran the wrong way and lost both shoes.

cards.q: Where did the four little rabbits live?
cards.note: In the book they live in a sand bank under the roots of a very big fir tree.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'mischief' mean?
cards.note: Getting into mischief is doing naughty things; it is Potter's own word.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
